channel.title: World News
channel.description: Aggregated headlines linking to original publishers

item.title: Malaysia's unwanted refugees: The plight of the Rohingya
item.description: On November 19, the International Court of Justice delivered a historic ruling: finding Myanmar guilty of committing genocide against the Rohingya in 2017. Malaysia has long been a supporter of the persecuted Muslim minority. But its role as a safe haven is coming to an end, amid a rise in hate speech and calls for the expulsion of Rohingya via social media.

item.title: Italy strike draws workers, students into nationwide protests over wages and living costs
item.description: A nationwide strike was expected to disrupt schools, hospitals and local transport across Italy on Friday as workers and students began marching in dozens of cities to demand higher wages, lower living costs and greater social protections. The labor action coincided with an International Day of Student Mobilisation, with organisers planning demonstrations in more than 45 Italian cities. FRANCE 24's Seema Gupta reports from Rome, Italy.

item.title: South Africa: High Court examines asylum seekers' detention at Lindela centre
item.description: South Africa's High Court judges visited the Lindela Repatriation Centre in Krugersdorp this week, ahead of delivering a ruling on 33 urgent applications concerning the detention of asylum seekers. The court is examining conflicting interpretations of a Constitutional Court ruling that prohibits the deportation of asylum seekers whose claims are still being processed. The case comes amid a wider and increasingly tense debate over immigration in South Africa, which has at times spilled over into deadly xenophobic violence. FRANCE 24's Eunice Masson reports from Cape Town, South Africa.

item.title: 'Our culture and identity': Deaf Nigerians embrace indigenous sign languages
item.description: With a quick flick of the wrist, Umaru Zayyanu conveys the phrase "I am a Nigerian". But the 37-year-old is not signing, rather in the west African nation's official sign language. Instead, he's using Hausa sign language. Such indigenous sign languages abound in Africa's most populous country, where deaf people were communicating with each other long before the advent of formal sign language taught in deaf schools, in 1960.

item.title: Ghana's $60 million presidential jet purchase sparks controversy
item.description: Ghanaian President John Mahama is facing growing criticism over his government's recent purchase of a $60 million presidential jet. While in opposition, Mahama had criticised similar plans by the previous administration. The government in Accra is now defending the purchase, pointing to the country's improved economic situation. It argues that the question was never whether the ageing presidential aircraft should be replaced, but rather when the timing would be right. FRANCE 24's Justice Baidoo reports.

item.title: Army postpones plan to detonate nearly 10,000 pounds of lead azide until Monday
item.description: Two rapid controlled detonations scheduled to take place at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant in Middletown on Friday have been postponed by three days.

item.title: Senate passes bipartisan energy bill amid environmental concerns
item.description: As Americans struggle with rising energy costs and increased demand driven by AI, the Senate passed a bipartisan bill that will speed up the approval process for data centers and power plants.

item.title: France awaits verdict in landmark police brutality trial over Michel Zecler assault
item.description: A French prosecutor on Thursday urged a court to jail three policemen who beat up a black music producer to four to six years, in a rare case of alleged police brutality to go to criminal court. The assault on Michel Zecler, now 47, triggered renewed outrage in France over police violence, which victims and researchers say is systemic but authorities and law enforcement unions claim is limited to isolated cases. The prosecutor argued the case had caused "immense harm to Michel Zecler but also to society as a whole," and that those on trial had "betrayed" their uniform.

item.title: Was the historic Shenzhen summit a political win or humiliation for Putin?
item.description: The world watched with bated breath Thursday as the presidents of China, Russia and the United States met for 90 minutes for an unprecedented trilateral summit in Shenzhen. Each leader came to the negotiating table with their own motivations. But Russia's Vladimir Putin was seen as walking away worse off than his counterparts, with some media outlets reporting the Kremlin leader was "humiliated" during the talks.

item.title: Rare EU-UK summit as Andy Burnham seeks to mend Brexit damage
item.description: UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham and the EU's top officials were set to announce deals to ease trade and youth mobility at a Brussels summit Friday, billed as a first step in a push to rebuild ties after Brexit. But in a potential spoiler for Burnham's "reset", Brussels said the deals coming into force would be conditional on reaching an agreement to cut university fees for EU students in Britain. FRANCE 24's International Affairs Editor Rochelle Ferguson Bouyahi tells us more.

item.title: 'Coalition of the Willing': Ukraine's allies meet in Berlin after Trump-Putin-Xi talks
item.description: Ukraine's allies met Thursday for a "Coalition of the Willing" summit in Berlin with President Volodymyr Zelensky to stress solid wartime support for Kyiv and to push for a European role in any future peace talks. The meeting – co-hosted by the leaders of Germany, France and Britain – was being held shortly after unprecedented three-way talks in China between US President Donald Trump, Russia's Vladimir Putin and China's Xi Jinping.

item.title: Spain's leaders clash over corruption, economy in tense election debate
item.description: Spain's Socialist Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez acknowledged making "mistakes" as he faced off with his main conservative rival in a key debate on Thursday before an election next week that could leave the far right on the cusp of power. The pair clashed over the economy, housing, immigration, corruption, foreign policy, as well as policies towards women, repeatedly interrupting each other during the live televised showdown.

item.title: Poland says Russian missile hit its territory during attack on Ukraine
item.description: Poland on Friday said that no one was hurt after a Russian missile hit southeast Poland during an attack on Ukraine. Polish authorities earlier said they were investigating reports that at ​least two unknown objects had fallen near the border with Ukraine.

item.title: Iraqi forces strike compromise with powerful pro-Iran militia
item.description: Iraq has reached ​a compromise with the powerful Iran-backed militia Kataib Hezbollah, three senior security officials said, after Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi readied security forces to move against the group. Iraqi officials had accused the group of running a smuggling ring that siphoned off hundreds of millions ​of dollars' worth of ‌state-owned oil. Under the deal brokered by senior Shi'ite political leaders to avert a confrontation, government ⁠forces were expected to move into the group's stronghold of Jurf al-Sakhar on Friday.

item.title: Outcry as fossil fuels scrubbed from draft UN climate deal
item.description: UN climate talks co-host Australia unveiled a new draft agreement Thursday that drops any mention of fossil fuels, the leading driver of global warming, sparking anger from campaign groups. The nearly 200 nations involved in the COP31 global climate talks in Turkey have until Friday to strike a final agreement, though the marathon negotiations often run into overtime. The summit is unfolding against a record-breaking El Nino, disasters fuelled by climate change from Europe to Nepal and a global energy shock triggered by the Iran war.

item.title: DOJ dropping Alaska midterms Senate certification lawsuit, saying case is 'moot'
item.description: The Justice Department is giving up on its controversial lawsuit that sought to potentially block the certification of Alaska's U.S. Senate race.

item.title: Brussels, London eye 'reset' deal at Burnham's EU summit
item.description: British Prime Minister Andy Burnham is due to meet EU chiefs Ursula von der Leyen and Antonio Costa in Brussels on Friday for a summit aimed at resetting ties after the turbulent years surrounding Brexit. The two sides are hoping to strike several deals, with the talks expected to pave the way for closer cooperation in the future. FRANCE 24's Brussels correspondent Dave Keating explains the main issues on the agenda.

item.title: The far right is 'missing the butt' of the GTA VI joke: It's them!
item.description: PRESS REVIEW – Friday, November 20: We look at reactions to the historic summit in Shenzhen between Donald Trump, Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping. Also, COP31 heads into its final stretch, but fossil fuels have vanished from the draft deal. Plus, the Guardian features a long read on "Power Slapping". Finally, we look at a different kind of hobby: "Grand Theft Auto VI" is finally out.

item.title: New York City unveils a bold plan to move its jails off Rikers Island
item.description: New York City officials are moving forward with plans to close Rikers, the city's main jail complex, after years of discussion. The jail has been plagued by assaults and inmate deaths.

item.title: Critics are calling what brand-new release a masterpiece? The quiz knows
item.description: Plus: Are you up to date on your James Bond news? If so, you'll get at least one question right.

item.title: How exactly did Trump get so rich on crypto? We explain
item.description: President Trump has made billions of dollars in his second term — most of it in cryptocurrencies. Democrats are vowing to probe his businesses as they gear up to take over Congress next year.

item.title: Former French prime minister Dominique de Villepin announces presidential bid
item.description: France’s former conservative prime minister Dominique de Villepin, who served as former president Jacques Chirac’s foreign minister during the country’s steadfast opposition to the US-led invasion of Iraq in 2003, formally launched his presidential campaign Friday. But while De Villepin’s opposition to Israel’s Gaza campaign and assured analysis of international affairs has caught the eyes of younger voters, it remains to be seen if he can persuade them to cast a ballot for him.

item.title: The U.K. and EU hold a rare summit to strengthen ties
item.description: A decade after the people of Britain voted to leave the European Union, top EU officials are meeting with Prime Minister Andy Burnham on Friday, looking to mend more fences.

item.title: Iraqi security forces deploy in Hezbollah stronghold under compromise deal
item.description: Iraqi security forces deployed ​in the Kataib Hezbollah stronghold of Jurf al-Sakhar, state media said on Friday, under a compromise deal brokered by Shi'ite politicians. Iraq's prime minister ordered a security intervention earlier this week after accusing the Iran-backed militia of smuggling state-owned oil worth ⁠hundreds of millions of dollars.

item.title: Europe's youth set to join mass cost of living protests in 25 countries
item.description: Youth protests are set to take place in more than 25 countries in Europe on Friday and over the weekend, coalition organisers said, as demostrators seek to increase pressure on governments over issues including soaring housing costs and deteriorating learning conditions with a show of cross-border solidarity.

item.title: Households stockpiling 'emergency items' boosts retail sales
item.description: Shoppers appear to be heeding government warnings to stock-up on essentials amid a surprise leap in retail sales.

item.title: Live: Russia fired than 100 missiles overnight in 'one of largest attacks ever', Zelensky says
item.description: Russia fired more than 100 missiles at Ukraine overnight in "one of the largest attacks" ever, President Volodymr Zelensky said on Friday, killing eight and wounding 28 others. The fresh wave of missile and drone attacks came after Russian President Vladimir Putin vowed a "painful" retaliation after Ukraine this week damaged the Crimea bridge. Follow our liveblog for the latest updates.

item.title: Infantino, Tashima and Diallo officially enter FIFA presidential race
item.description: Three candidates have officially submitted their bids for the FIFA presidency. Gianni Infantino, who has been in office for 11 years, is seeking a fourth consecutive term. Backed by UEFA, French Football Federation president Philippe Diallo wants to offer an alternative to Infantino’s leadership. He will face Japan’s Kozo Tashima, honorary president of the Japan Football Association. The election will take place on March 18, 2027 in Rabat, Morocco.

item.title: Czechs protest en masse against 'concentration of power in one hand' and growing control over media
item.description: As large demonstrations in the Czech Republic challenge Prime Minister Andrej Babiš's plans to change the funding model of public broadcasters, Mikuláš Minář, Chair of the Million Moments for Democracy movement, joins François Picard from Prague for Spotlight, warning that his country risks following Hungary and Slovakia in democratic backsliding. "We are really afraid that the Czech Republic is following the Orbánian Hungarian way, (Fico's) Slovakian way," he says.

item.title: Trump-Putin-Xi meeting updates: Schumer calls trip a 'historical embarrassment'
item.description: Trump participated on Thursday in the first-ever trilateral meeting with Putin and Xi.

item.title: Man accused of killing British woman sent knife with her blood on to friend
item.description: A man accused of murdering a British woman he met on a fetish website sent a knife with her blood on it to a friend, a US court has heard.

item.title: EU and UK set to sign deals on trade, energy, youth mobility at Brussels summit
item.description: The UK and the EU are poised to agree new deals on trade, energy and youth mobility at a summit in Brussels on Friday, as part of UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham's bid to reset ties with the bloc. Burnham – who has said he hopes to see Britain rejoin the EU in his lifetime – argues the deals will help fix some of the damage Brexit inflicted.

item.title: WATCH: Motorcyclist survives after fiery crash with Tesla
item.description: A motorcyclist walked away from a fiery crash on an L.A. freeway after suddenly being cut off by a Tesla in the left lane.

item.title: Trump China trip: Iran and Ukraine not in 'peace declaration' and more takeaways
item.description: Trump heads back to Washington after meeting with Xi and Putin -- the first sitdown between the three superpowers -- with no tangible diplomatic breakthroughs in hand.

item.title: Trump pardons late baseball great Pete Rose after historic China trip
item.description: On the way back from his Asia trip, President Donald Trump said Thursday he issued a "complete and total pardon" to baseball legend Pete Rose, who died in 2024.

item.title: Met Police can photograph people without consent in facial recognition pilot
item.description: Police officers in London will be able to use their mobile phones to photograph and identify suspects without their consent as part of a new facial recognition pilot.

item.title: Anti-monarchy group hands over 'evidence' on Andrew as it calls for investigation
item.description: An anti-monarchy campaign group says it has given police and the Crown Prosecution Service "evidence" on Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor.

item.title: Why the U.S. air traffic control system still relies on an 'antique' network
item.description: The FAA says the telecom outage that led to Friday's nationwide ground stop began with an upgrade to fiber-optic cables. Industry experts say the work is long overdue.

item.title: England handed suspended away ticket ban for fans' chants during Spain win
item.description: England have been given a suspended away ticket ban by UEFA for "racist and/or discriminatory behaviour" by their fans during a match with Spain in Madrid on Sunday.

item.title: Thomas Markle fit to stand trial over child abuse images, US court rules
item.description: Thomas Markle is fit to stand trial on charges of possessing child sexual abuse material, a US court has ruled.

item.description: President Donald Trump announced "major combat operations" against Iran on Feb. 28.

item.title: UK conducting offensive cyber ops against Russia, China, Iran and North Korea, says top commander
item.description: The UK is conducting offensive cyber operations against Russia, China, Iran and North Korea, a top military commander has for the first time revealed.

item.title: Trump’s CISA pick rejects Jan. 6 as an 'attack,' won't name 2020 election winner
item.description: Michael LoSapio, President Donald Trump's nominee to lead the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, says he doesn't consider the Jan_ 6 Capitol insurrection an "attack."

item.title: Judges have put Trump's arch and golf course on hold, but only for a matter of days
item.description: A federal judge has twice delayed construction of Trump's arch. Another is keeping East Potomac Park open. The proposed golf course redesign got mixed feedback from a federal arts panel on Thursday.

item.description: ABC News associate producer Ben Greenberg took a vacation day to play “Grand Theft Auto VI” and told Kyra Phillips about it live.

item.title: What Obama said to newly elected Democrats after midterm gains
item.description: Former President Barack Obama told Democratic U.S. House members-elect on Wednesday that they should value their ideological diversity even if they have disagreements.

item.title: Xi tells Trump US must do 'the right thing' over Taiwan to avoid 'great turbulence'
item.description: Chinese President Xi Jinping used his meeting with President Donald Trump in Shenzhen on Thursday to warn against the creation of "turbulence" over the issue of Taiwan.

item.title: Auditors concerned about billions ICE is spending to expand immigration detention
item.description: Federal auditors warn that ICE is spending billions of dollars to expand immigration detention without "determining the cost effectiveness" of new initiatives.

item.title: WATCH: Trump calls Putin, Xi his friends after meeting
item.description: Doug Lute, former U.S. ambassador to NATO, says President Donald Trump referring to Putin and Xi as friends is "concerning for America's allies."

item.description: How do we maintain healthy romantic relationships as we age? Allison Aubrey and Scott Detrow talk about about the science of healthy, later-in-life relationships.

item.description: Actor Kel Mitchell shares how he's using his star power to help families in need.

item.description: The EU has revealed it suffered a cyber attack powered by AI last month and some of its digital tools are still offline as a result.

item.title: WATCH: Military family gets surprise of a lifetime at 2026 CMAs
item.description: "GMA" sponsor Chevrolet teams up with rising country star Zach Top to surprise a military family.

item.title: WATCH: NASA's Voyager 1 now a light-day away after 1977 launch
item.description: NASA launched its Voyager 1 space probe in 1977. It's made it more than 16 billion miles in space, marking the farthest any human made object has ever traveled.

item.title: Burnham says Europe 'ready to enter negotiations' to help end Russia's war in Ukraine
item.description: Europe is ready to enter negotiations to help end Russia's war in Ukraine, Andy Burnham has said.

item.description: ABC News' Danny New talks to a woman in Oregon who helped reunite a missing cat with its owner in South Carolina.

item.description: FIFA has confirmed which candidates will stand in next year's presidential election - as UEFA challenges restrictions placed on documents relating to the World Cup sell-off scandal.

item.description: Rescuers are speaking out about the miraculous rescue of Isaac the cat after the deadly building collapse in Brooklyn.

item.description: Braden Peters is accused of giving alcohol to a teen and sexually assaulting her at his family's Cape Cod home.

item.description: Dozens of displaced Palestinians have fled their tents and shelters in central ‌Gaza after Israel launched a rare ground operation in an area it had left under a ceasefire last year.

item.description: ABC News legal analyst Brian Buckmire and correspondent Alex Stone explain what prosecutors are arguing differently and the potential sentence if the man is convicted at his federal retrial.

item.description: New York Gov. Kathy Hochul is demanding information from ICE and a Virginia-based construction company about a new tent immigration detention facility set to house women.

item.description: The Prince and Princess of Wales met the prime minister of India on Wednesday to discuss trade and bilateral ‌ties at the end of their three-day visit to the country.

item.description: Senate Banking Committee Chairman Tim Scott, a Republican, sent letters to both Huang and Lutnick to publicly testify in front of the committee

item.description: ABC News' Danny New talks to a mother in England whose family dog's actions helped alert her that her baby boy had a congenital heart condition.

item.description: ABC News' Will Reeve visits Lincoln Financial Field to meet neurodivergent employees helping make Philadelphia Eagles game days special through the team's commitment to autism inclusion.
